content.title: About
content.content: Celery (Apium graveolens) is a crisp, juicy vegetable with long, ribbed stalks and leafy tops, native to the Mediterranean and southern Europe. It has a fresh, slightly salty, herbal flavor and a crunchy texture. Celery is eaten raw as a snack, in salads, and juices, and cooked in soups, stews, and stocks as a basic flavoring.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Celery is related to parsley, carrots, and fennel, and celeriac is a root variety of the same species.
Celery seeds are used as a spice and in celery salt.
Celery, onion, and carrot form the base of many classic soups and sauces.
Both celery stalks and leaves are edible.

items.title: Hydrating and low in calories
items.content: Celery is mostly water and very low in calories.

items.title: Provides vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K supports normal blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains potassium and folate
items.content: These nutrients support normal blood pressure and cell function.

items.title: Contains plant compounds
items.content: Celery contains flavonoids such as apigenin and luteolin with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Celery contributes fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: Celery allergy
items.content: Celery allergy can be serious, including in cooked celery and celery seed, and celery is a recognized major food allergen in many countries.

items.title: Possible medication interactions
items.content: Celery contains vitamin K. People taking blood thinners should consult a healthcare professional about keeping their intake consistent.

items.title: Sun sensitivity
items.content: Celery contains compounds that can make skin more sensitive to sunlight in rare cases.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Wash celery thoroughly, since conventionally grown celery may carry residues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Celery can be eaten raw with dips, peanut butter, or hummus, chopped into salads, or blended into juices and smoothies. It is sautéed or simmered in soups, stews, stocks, stuffing, and braises. The leaves can be used as an herb.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store celery in the refrigerator, wrapped in foil or in a container with a little water, where it usually keeps for one to two weeks. Keep cut celery in an airtight container. Celery that is limp can sometimes be revived in cold water.
